RecordThing.Description:
The Norsec TTY-6 'Teletype' is a free-standing serial terminal - desk unit, monitor and keyboard - with no processor and no storage: a 40x20 character display and a keyboard controller wired to a 7-register serial UART. Any {THING:StructureCircuitHousing;IC Housing} can drive it with the get and put instructions.
Registers: 0 DATA (put: print a character by Unicode code point, e.g. $2588; get: pop the next typed character, 0 if none - or a packed 6-character string per access in buffered mode), 1 STRING (put: print a packed 6-character string, e.g. put d0 1 STR("HELLO "); get: peek next typed character), 2 COUNT (get: characters waiting in the 256-byte input buffer), 3 CONTROL (put 1: clear screen, 2: flush input, 3: clear the overflow flag, 4/5: output unbuffered/buffered, 6/7: input unbuffered/buffered, 8/9: local echo off/on; get: status bits), 4 ROW and 5 COL (cursor address, read/write), 6 COLOR (pen colour for newly printed characters: the standard logic colour values 0-11, e.g. Color.Red, or -1 for the default green; read/write). Every character keeps the colour it was printed with - changing the pen never recolours existing text.
Control codes: 8 backspace, 10 line feed, 12 clear screen, 13 carriage return, 127 destructive backspace, 133 new line (CR+LF). Memory is volatile: switching the terminal off or cutting its power wipes the screen, input buffer and every mode. Writing the Setting logic variable prints a packed string. Quantity reports input waiting, Error reports input-buffer overflow. Click the screen to type: each keystroke is placed directly in the input buffer (Enter sends 13, Backspace sends 8). The terminal is full duplex by default - nothing is displayed unless the circuit prints it. In half duplex (put 3 9) the keyboard echoes typed characters to the screen immediately, without circuit involvement.
This kit places a Norsec TTY-6 Serial Terminal, a free-standing monitor-and-keyboard computer block readable and writable by IC10 circuits.
